label: final copy step of length-3 sequences
explanation: Fires almost only in the copy phase of L=3 sequences, at t=5. That is the last output step, where the model has just been fed back original token 1 (prev2 = <DEL>) and has to output original token 2. This one condition holds 93% of activation mass, with precision 0.97 on dev. Never fires in the original or delimiter phases, or on the first occurrence of a token. The misses (7% of mass) are weak activations: the step before (t=4) in L=3 sequences, and scattered late copy steps in long sequences (L=6-9, mostly the last or second-to-last output). The strongest examples tend to begin with c/d/a, and the inactive L=3 cases often begin with h/r/t/k/p, so the first original token may modulate magnitude, but this was not checked quantitatively.

issues: Dataset mismatch: the user asked to run the baseline on features/copy_transcoder_v2_1of5. That directory holds raw seq .pt files plus a subsample manifest, not an autointerp store, so this verdict, like the original, comes from features/copy_gru_v1_neuron_baseline_store. The 1/5 subsample has not been analyzed yet.

All reported test numbers reproduce exactly: P 0.974, R 0.752, F1 0.848, mass recall 0.929. On the dev split it is never active in the original or delimiter phase, or when in_first==1. 93% of mass is at t=5 and 93.6% in L=3.
The low recall (25% of active steps missed) is made up of weak activations, only 7.1% of mass. The predicate catches 99% of the top two activation quartiles but only 22.5% of the bottom quartile.
A small systematic subclass the explanation misses: at t=4 in L=3, the unit fires reliably when the first token is '0' (precision 0.67 over 82 steps). Adding it only raises F1 from 0.848 to 0.855.
The L=9, t=17 last-output-step activity (12% rate, 2.2% of mass) can't be added cheaply: it drops F1 to 0.24.

The claim that the first token modulates magnitude is weak. When the first token is h/r/t/k/p, precision at L3/t5 is 0.952 against 0.974 overall, a minor effect. The explanation correctly marked it as unverified.
